newsitem.title: FRANCE: Saudi Arabia concludes 800,000 T barley deal-trade.
newsitem.headline: Saudi Arabia concludes 800,000 T barley deal-trade.

text.p: Saudi Arabia has concluded a deal to buy some 800,000 tonnes of feed barley from the world market, with the European Union grabbing the lion's share, grain traders said on Friday.
Exporters also believe Saudi Arabia, the world's biggest importer of feed barley, may be back in the market soon to take advantage of decling world prices.
"The deal is done and it is for 800,000 tonnes, of which at least 600,000 tonnes will come from the EU," one trader said.
Saudi Arabia had kept world markets guessing over its purchase plans since news of a deal emerged more than two weeks ago.
Traders initially said it had bought a provisional 800,000 tonnes of barley at prices ranging from $160 to $162 per tonne, including cost, insurance and freight.
But the industry had been awaiting confirmation amid reports the quantity might have been reduced to 600,000 tonnes.
The EU was expected to provide the bulk of the grain as it enjoys a supply and freight advantage over other producers.
Traders now say the EU should provide at least 600,000 tonnes of barley, with one or two cargoes coming from the U.S. and/or Canada.
Subtracting freight costs, the equivalent FOB price for the purchase stood around $142-145 per tonne.
The EU had signalled it would not part from its barley for less than $149 FOB when news of the deal broke.

But as world prices slipped on prospects of a strong world crop, the EU softened its position, selling 234,324 tonnes of barley at around $145 FOB on Aug 29 and 183,411 tonnes at around $142 on September 5.
Worried about losing market share to rivals whose crops will come in soon, the EU has also increased to 600,000 tonnes the allocation of German intervention barley available for exports.
Traders estimate Saudi Arabia's import needs for 1996/97 at 400,000 tonnes a month, and believe the kingdom may tap world markets again for barley in October if prices continue to decline.
In its latest report, the International Grains Council said Saudi Arabia might import 3.5 million tonnes of barley in 1996/97 against an estimated 3.2 million in 1995/96.
